summary.description: The Clergyman joins a fragile circle of trust.
rules: A Clergyman knows anyone who is also a Clergyman.
However, if any Clergyman dies for any reason, the others might die as well.
Whenever a Clergyman dies, any number of other living Clergymen may die as well. This may happen immediately, or that night.

howToRun: During setup, include between two to three Clergyman tokens in the bag.
During the first night, wake each Clergyman. Point to all other Clergymen.
If a Clergyman dies, you may choose to have any number of other living Clergyman die immediately, or that night. Mark any chosen player *DEAD*.
examples: Ada, Ben, and Cara are Clergymen. Each starts knowing the other two. When Ben is executed, Cara dies that night, but Ada is left alive.
Two Clergymen are in play. One is killed by the Demon, and the other also dies before dawn.
A Pit-Hag creates a new Clergyman. The new Clergyman learns the existing Clergymen that night. The original Clergymen receive no new information.
tipsAndTricks: You all know each other, and you all know each other's information. You don't need to coordinate to make this work.
You are likely to be built as an evil team. If you are being framed and executed, expect one of you to die immediately to clear the other.
opposingTips: You can't bluff Clergyman alone. Plan in advance who your other Clergymen will be.

summary.description: The Shepherd risks their life to identify the Demon.
rules: Each night except the first, the Shepherd chooses one Demon character.
If that character is in play, the Shepherd dies. A dead Demon character is still in play. A Demon previously in play, but changed by the Pit-Hag, is not.
The Shepherd observes only whether they survive. They must deduce whether they died to their own ability, or something else.

howToRun: Each night except the first, wake the Shepherd. They indicate one Demon character. Put the Shepherd to sleep.
If the chosen character is in play, mark the Shepherd *DEAD*. Otherwise, nothing happens.
howToRunExamples: Yes, But Don't use the Recluse to alter the outcome. An Outsider's effect, including replacing a Townsfolk, should be about one third as bad as having a Minion. The Shepherd only does one thing, and blanking them exceeds this budget.
examples: The Shepherd chooses Imp while an Imp is in play. The Shepherd dies that night.
The Fang Gu has died after creating a new Fang Gu, which the Pit-Hag turns into a No Dashii. The Shepherd chooses Fang Gu, and dies because the dead Fang Gu remains in play.
The Shepherd correctly chooses the Vortox but is protected by the Innkeeper. They live, and cannot tell whether their guess was wrong or their death was prevented.
tipsAndTricks: Go for the most impactful Demon characters first! Discovering a Vortox, Lleech, or Fang Gu early can be game solving!
opposingTips: Your only information is a signal when you die, but you can claim to have ruled out Demon types. But if you're alive at the end, people are unlikely to trust your information.

summary.description: The Joe is able to get themself executed at any time, allowing them to prevent any execution.
rules: If at least 5 non-Traveller players live and the Joe publicly claims to be Joe, they are executed before the end of the day.
The Joe may claim at any time as long as all players and the Storyteller are present.
If the Joe has publicly claimed, they must be executed before dusk.

howToRun: If five or more non-Traveller players are alive and the Joe publicly claims to be the Joe, mark them *CLAIMED*.
At any time before dusk, execute the marked Joe. When this happens, end the day normally. No other execution can occur that day.
examples: There are 5 players alive. The Shabaloth is about to be executed with 4 votes, the Joe publicly claims Joe. They are immediately executed and die.
At the start of day 1, the Joe publicly claims Joe. Later that day after allowing public abilities to be used, the Storyteller declares that the Joe is executed and dies.
tipsAndTricks: Save your ability for when your team is in trouble. You can safely replace any execution. Save an ally!
Use your ability to frame someone! Players expect you to protect evil. If you use your ability to replace the execution of a Demon candidate, you could waste 2 days of executions.
opposingTips: Try to work out why the Joe chose to end the day early. You gain a lot of information if you can work out whether they are trying to prevent a specific execution.

When a player is executed for claiming Joe, they are now confirmed to be evil. Make use of this when trying to deduce other evil players. Anyone who would require the Joe to be good for them to be evil is now verifiably good.
